result.summary: Ensure all initial outbound connections (default 3) for private transaction broadcast complete even if the transaction is received back from the network or conflicted before completion. Replace immediate transaction removal upon network receipt with a resolved flag, preventing additional retry connections via TryGrantRetry while allowing pending initial sends to finish. Remove DidNodeConfirmReception in favor of checking whether the connection completed its handshake before scheduling compensation attempts.
result.problem: When a privately broadcast transaction was received back from the network or became invalid in the mempool before all initial connections finished, the node immediately removed the transaction and canceled any remaining unestablished connections. This introduced a timing side channel where adversaries returning a transaction quickly could suppress remaining outbound connections and correlate broadcasts.
evidence: PR description states this is 'addressing the theoretical timing attack described in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34707#issuecomment-5603256702' and 'fixes theoretical timing attacks described in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29415#discussion_r2035693786'
Author notes this is intended as an alternative approach to PR #34707
result.changed_since_previous: No substantial changes to the approach; includes minor refinements to tests and connection lifecycle cleanup in PrivateBroadcast::Add.
result.card: Ensures all three initial outbound connections for private transaction broadcasts finish even if the transaction is received back from the network while connections are still pending. Previously, receiving the transaction back immediately canceled unstarted broadcast connections, introducing theoretical timing side channels that an adversary could exploit to detect or link private broadcasts. The change marks transactions resolved to prevent retries without truncating the initial batch, and replaces receipt tracking upon peer disconnect with handshake status.

risk.why: Bugs in managing outbound private broadcast connections or message processing could lead to connection exhaustion, failed broadcasts, or unexpected peer disconnect behavior.
